Directions Along Which the Estimate Does Not Exist

Source: R/separation.R
separation_diagnosis.Rd

Searches the coefficients of a fit for a direction of recession, along which the penalized log-likelihood keeps increasing, or stays level, as the linear predictors move without bound. Such a direction exists when the maximum likelihood estimate does not exist (separation in a binary or binomial response, a level of a factor with all its counts at zero, a group without zeros in the equation of a zero-inflation probability), and the fit then stops at a finite point that depends only on its stopping rule.

Usage

separation_diagnosis(
  fit,
  steps = 2^(0:6),
  tol = 1e-08,
  flat = 1e-06,
  max_eigen = 4L
)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

steps

The multiples of the scaled direction at which the objective is evaluated, in units of the linear predictor.

tol

The largest rise of the objective, relative to \(\max(1, |F(\hat\beta)|)\), that is still read as level.

flat

The largest ratio of an eigenvalue to the largest one at which an eigenvector of \(S\) against \(M\) is probed beside the Newton step.

max_eigen

The largest number of eigenvectors that are probed.

Value

A list with found (logical, a direction of recession), descent (logical, a direction of descent), directions (one entry per direction found, each with kind, "recession" or "descent"; coefficients, the named components of the direction over the coefficients that it moves, scaled so that the largest change in a linear predictor is one; free, the names of those coefficients that carry no smooth penalty; equations; n_moved, the number of observations whose linear predictor moves by more than 1e-3 in each equation; change, the change of the objective at each step; source, "newton" or "eigen"; and curvature, the curvature along the direction against \(M\) as a ratio to the largest eigenvalue), newton_eta, the largest change that the Newton step makes in a linear predictor, min_eigen, the smallest ratio of an eigenvalue of \(S\) to the largest one, n_eval, the number of evaluations of the objective, and reason, a character string where the check could not be made.

Details

The objective is \(F\) of statmod_objective(), at the fitted hyperparameters, with gradient \(g\) and Hessian \(K\). The coefficients are split into those that carry no smooth penalty (\(u\)) and those that do (\(v\)), and the latter are profiled out through the Schur complement \(S = K_{uu} - K_{uv} K_{vv}^{-1} K_{vu}\), so that the eigenvalue problem has the size of the unpenalized coefficients whatever the number of random effects. A penalized coefficient moves along each candidate as the profile requires, \(v = -K_{vv}^{-1} K_{vu} u\), and only the null space of a penalty can carry a direction of recession.

The candidates are the Newton step at the fitted point, \(\delta = -K^{-1} g\), with each eigenvalue of \(S\) floored at \(10^{-14}\) times the largest; where coefficients are estimated on the outer criterion, a second Newton step that keeps their gradient in \(F\) (see below); and both signs of the eigenvectors of \(S\) against the metric of the linear predictors, \(M = X_u^\top X_u\) over the equations, whose eigenvalues fall below flat times the largest one. At a point where the fit has drifted along a direction of recession the gradient and the curvature along it vanish together, so the Newton step remains of order one in the linear predictor while the decrease that it predicts is below the stopping rule.

Each candidate \(d\) is scaled so that the largest change it makes in a linear predictor is one, and \(F\) is evaluated at \(\hat\beta + t d\) for every t in steps. A candidate is a direction of recession when \(F\) does not rise by more than tol times \(\max(1, |F(\hat\beta)|)\) at any of those points, nor from one point to the next, and the whole decrease stays within mode_error_limit(). It is a direction of descent when \(F\) falls by more than mode_error_limit() at one of them, which means that the point is not a minimum at all (a scale whose group has a constant response, where the log-likelihood is unbounded, is an example). At an ordinary optimum a change of one in a linear predictor already raises \(F\).

Coefficients held at the kink of a penalty, those of a block that is a working linearization (frozen_block()) and aliased coefficients are held fixed. Coefficients estimated on the outer criterion move with the others, since a direction of recession of \(F\) is one of that criterion too when no random effect integrates over them, but their gradient in \(F\) is set to zero, because they sit at the root of the outer criterion and not of \(F\). For the same reason a direction of descent is read on the change of \(F\) after removing the linear term of those coordinates, \(t\,g_m^\top d\), where \(g_m\) is their gradient in \(F\): under reml() the scale of a gaussian is not at the minimum of \(F\), and without the correction the difference between the two criteria reads as a direction of descent. A direction of recession is read on \(F\) itself.
